page: Vultr vhf-16c-58gb is a virtual server belonging to the High Frequency Compute family. It features an Intel x86_64 architecture with 16 shared vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The processor operates at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz and is equipped with 32 KB L1d cache, 4 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. The system is configured with 58.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 3.62 GB of RAM per core, and includes a bundled 1024 GB NVMe SSD for local storage.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average performance across standard compute and cryptographic operations. The single-core stress-ng CPU score is 1884.79, while the multi-core score reaches 14058.95. Cryptographic capabilities are supported by hardware-accelerated AES, resulting in a PassMark CPU encryption test score of 5232.56. However, memory bandwidth exhibits constraints under heavy loads, with large-block read bandwidth dropping to a weak 24.85 GB/sec and write bandwidth registering a poor 13.66 GB/sec. Static web serving throughput is also relatively low at 6.08 GB/sec.

Given the shared CPU allocation and the balance of 16 vCPUs to 58.0 GB RAM, this server offers a cost-efficient profile for general-purpose workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated CPU performance. It is well-suited for database operations, as evidenced by a PassMark database score of 5215.72 and a Redis SET throughput of 11.03 million operations per second. Other appropriate workloads include multi-threaded decompression tasks, basic web serving, and lightweight language model inference using small models.
